source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
a. Create a standardized electrical safety inspection checklist that includes all relevant areas of inspection (e.g., power cables, plugs, internal components, heat emissions, casing for cracks or damage, grounding, insulation, and functionality).

3. Document the specific model, make, serial number, and any additional identifying information of the appliance being inspected.

4. Record the date and time of the safety check, and include the name(s) of the person(s) conducting the test.

5. Use the checklist to guide the inspection process. Examine each part and function of the appliance, marking checks, or notes against each listed item.

6. For each fault discovered:
   - Describe the nature of the problem (e.g., frayed power cable, sparks, overheating, abnormal noise, or short-circuiting).
   - Detail the exact location of the fault (e.g., "The power cable is frayed approximately 2 inches from the plug").
